critique: The render passes both acceptance tests. ISO shows an open, fully populated eight-lane board with no opaque block swallowing a subsystem; TOP confirms eight blue BRAM banks, both white FIFO capsules, the copper DSP multiplier column as a vertical row of dots, the brass twiddle feeder/rail L, the dark reduction spine pair, and the right-edge control cluster; SIDE shows the exploded butterfly lane riding on its two risers and the elevated routing channels; FRONT shows the seven-fin exploded heatsink lifted on its stub. The only real residual defect carried from the prior pass was geometric: of the three overhead routing channels only the return bus was grounded, leaving the brass twiddle broadcast rail and the copper operand-read bus reading as floating lines in the SIDE/FRONT elevations. That is now fixed with two short standoff posts, so all three channels read as physical wiring tied to the array frame.
changelog: Added twiddle_post: a short welded-steel standoff in the central lane-3/4 gap (x=-1.1, z=0) grounding the brass twiddle broadcast rail down onto the open array frame, so the twiddle fan-out no longer floats in the elevation views

Added read_post: a short copper standoff (x=-1.6, z=0) tying the elevated operand-read bus down onto the array frame between its crossbar seat and the multiplier-column arrow, completing the physical support of the read/twiddle/return triad
Wired both new posts into the connection graph (bu_array_base -> twiddle_post -> twiddle_rail; bu_array_base -> read_post -> read_bus) so the scene stays rooted with no dangling ids
Both posts placed at z=0 in the empty central gap so they cross no lane and occlude no multiplier/operator in plan or ISO
